name: Data Encrypted for Impact
summary: An adversary may encrypt files stored on a mobile device to prevent the user from accessing them. This may be done in order to extract monetary compensation from a victim in exchange for decryption or a decryption key (ransomware) or to render data permanently inaccessible in cases where the key is not saved or transmitted.

strategies.name: Detection of Data Encrypted for Impact

analytics.name: Analytic 1781
analytics.guidance: For Android, detect Data Encrypted for Impact by correlating analyst-visible device/network evidence and management state; use streaming or batched telemetry only where the documented collector is deployed. Correlate Application Permission via Android Enterprise DPC / Application Vetting [DevicePolicyManager.getPermissionGrantState(); PackageManager manifest/requested-permission review]; Application State via Android Enterprise / EMM [Managed package inventory/status and package metadata]; OS API Execution via Application Vetting / Instrumented Dynamic Analysis [Dynamic API/runtime trace: ContentResolver, DocumentProvider, StorageAccessFramework, or bulk stream I/O invocations exceed…

log_sources.name: android:EMM
log_sources.channel: Managed package inventory/status and package metadata

log_sources.name: mobile:DynamicAnalysis
log_sources.channel: Dynamic API/runtime trace: ContentResolver, DocumentProvider, StorageAccessFramework, or bulk stream I/O invocations exceed $FileModificationRateThreshold$ operations per minute across distinct file paths — API-level operation rate distinguishes ransomware from norma

log_sources.name: android:DevicePolicyManager
log_sources.channel: DevicePolicyManager policy/compliance/security-state queries and SecurityLog events where supported

evidence.description: Xbot can encrypt the victim's files in external storage (e.g., SD card) and then request a PayPal cash card as ransom.
